neighbours.label: temperature or colour class of a star (cooler, hottest, orange, O-type)
fire: Proxima Centauri is a red dwarf, much cooler than the Sun.
Blue B-type stars burn far hotter than yellow ones.
Aldebaran is an orange giant that is cooler than our Sun.
The host star is a little hotter and brighter than the Sun.
Rigel is one of the hottest bright stars in the winter sky.
The planet circles a small, cool K-type star.
Red giants are cooler at the surface but enormous in size.
Sirius is a white A-type star, hotter than the Sun.
quiet: Proxima Centauri is about four light years away from the Sun.
Bright stars were used by sailors to find their way at night.
Aldebaran is easy to find near the Pleiades in winter.
The host star is a little older and farther away than we thought.
Rigel is one of the brightest stars in the winter sky.
The planet circles its star once every twelve days.
Red giants were first studied in detail in the last century.
Sirius is the brightest star visible from Earth at night.

notes: Probes: 'O-type ... hottest' 0.90, 'slightly cooler ... than our Sun' 0.53, 'orange giant' 0.38; 'cooler' coffee 0.02, 'older' star 0.10.
